title: Macro-MoE JEV Router & OpenRouter Micro-Tier: Zero-Token Latent Task Routing and Frontier Quota Shielding
target_platform: Project Sanctuary task dispatch substrate, context/kernel.py, plugins/sanctuary-core, OpenRouter micro-tier API, and local MLX fallback
interest_statement: Deploy a zero-token Latent Decision-Tree Router (JEV) coupled with a low-cost OpenRouter micro-model tier (0.5B-3B) to eliminate local Mac storage/RAM bottlenecks, slash operational token burn, and strictly shield precious frontier subscriptions (Claude Sonnet, Codex, Gemini Argon) for high-leverage architectural and epistemic tasks.
hypothesis: A 2-stage hierarchical Macro-MoE routing architecture—comprising (1) a zero-token non-generative Joint-Embedding Vector (JEV) decision-tree router (<3ms latency) and (2) an OpenRouter micro-tier (0.5B-3B models) for mechanical and syntactic tasks—will successfully route and resolve >=80% of routine engineering tasks (linting, JSON formatting, test boilerplate, inbox triage) without invoking frontier models, reducing weekly frontier quota consumption by >=70% and task dispatch latency by >=60% compared to monolithic LLM routing, while maintaining a <=1% misrouting rate to frontier tiers.
falsification_criteria: FALSIFIED if: (1) the JEV router misclassifies >5% of complex architectural tasks into the micro-tier, causing execution failure; (2) the OpenRouter micro-tier achieves <75% first-pass pass-rate on mechanical formatting/linting tasks; (3) the net operational cost exceeds $15/month under continuous agentic loop execution; or (4) local Mac SSD/RAM footprint increases by >500MB (falsifying the local hardware preservation premise).
baseline_evidence: Observed in Project Sanctuary operational telemetry: (a) Every routine task dispatch currently invokes frontier LLMs (Claude Sonnet / Codex / Gemini Argon) or spins up the local 7B Qwen MLX model, consuming ~4.5GB RAM and burning expensive subscription quota on mechanical JSON formatting and linting. (b) arXiv:2610.39302 proves compact embedding encoders (109M) converge to the shared Platonic task manifold with 42x higher sample efficiency than next-token LLMs. (c) Live empirical tests on 2026-11-10 verified OpenRouter micro-tier connectivity: Llama-3.2-1B ($0.00000203/call, 0.62s), Llama-3.2-3B ($0.00000412/call, 0.24s), and Qwen3-Coder-Flash ($0.00001638/call, 0.58s); batch total $0.00002253 across 3 tasks.
experiment: Phase 1: Latent task topology profiling (build vector benchmark of 100 historical Sanctuary tasks). Phase 2: Implement prototype JEV decision-tree classifier using Apple Silicon Neural Engine / CoreML or lightweight embedding cosine projections. Phase 3: Build OpenRouter micro-tier client in sanctuary-core with failover to local MLX. Phase 4: Benchmark routing accuracy, latency, and quota shielding across a 50-task test matrix.
phases: Latent Task Topology Profiling & Dataset Construction
Benchmark Routing Accuracy, Latency, and Frontier Quota Shielding
score_basis: Leverage 5: fundamentally re-architects Sanctuary task dispatch, eliminates token waste, shields frontier quotas. Depth 4: operationalizes Platonic latent task classification and multi-tier routing. Cost 0.25: lightweight cloud micro-models ($10/mo) and deterministic Python router. Friction 2: standard API and lightweight embedding inference. Priority = (5*4)/(0.25*2) = 40.0.
strategic_intent: Establish a lean, hierarchical Macro-MoE routing substrate that preserves frontier AI quotas and protects local Mac hardware.
design_constraints: JEV Router must execute in <5ms without generating autoregressive tokens
Third-party black-box auto-routers (e.g. openrouter/free) are strictly barred; all dispatches must be deterministically directed to pinned models via Sanctuary's in-process JEV router
Local hardware storage addition must remain strictly under 500MB total
OpenRouter cloud calls must strictly respect cost caps ($10/month hard ceiling, $0.50/day flexible target)
Frontier escalation must require explicit JEV confidence or test failure triggers
Deterministic offline fallback to MLX must be maintained when network is unreachable

readiness.assessment: PROPOSED. Theoretical foundations validated in arXiv:2610.39302 and LEARNING/research/jepa_and_macro_moe/argon_analysis.md. OpenRouter key provisioned in ~/.zshrc and live API connectivity verified across 3 micro-models. Companion repo PRs #759 and #760 merged upstream.

model_routing.frontier_escalation_condition: Architectural design, novel hypothesis formulation, or persistent contradiction alerts
model_routing.routing_guidance: Routing decision is performed by zero-token JEV router; execution dispatched to OpenRouter micro-tier; escalation to Claude/Codex/Argon only on high complexity.

evidence.details: In 50-task held-out benchmark (LEARNING/experiments/mission-070/results.json), Tier 0 in-process JEV Router achieved 0.252ms mean latency with 0 tokens consumed (Gate 1 PASS), 100% routing accuracy and 100% frontier quota shielding across 40 routine tasks with 0.0% misclassification of architectural tasks (Gate 2 PASS). OpenRouter micro-tier client with $10 hard cap achieved 90.0% first-pass pass-rate on live mechanical tasks at $0.0000088/task (Gate 3 PASS). Storage addition was 0 MB with zero model weights downloaded (Gate 4 PASS).

lessons_learned: 1B models lack sufficient token precision for code syntax edits and sorting, whereas 3B and 30B MoE achieve 100% precision at under $0.00002/task.
Zero-token in-process latent routing (JEV) evaluates in <0.3ms without consuming LLM context tokens.
Sanctuary Macro-MoE successfully shields frontier quotas while maintaining strict $10 budget boundaries.
